### api-gateway-api-key-request-must-contain-key-else-403

**Claim.** When a usage plan is associated with an API and API keys are enabled on API methods, every incoming request must contain an API key; API Gateway compares it with the keys in the usage plan, throttles on a match, and otherwise returns a 403 Forbidden response.

**Scope.** REST APIs, methods that require an API key.

### api-gateway-cors-non-simple-needs-preflight-options-mock

### api-gateway-throttling-429-too-many-requests-retry

**Claim.** When request submissions exceed the steady-state request rate and burst limits, API Gateway begins to throttle requests, clients may receive 429 Too Many Requests error responses, and the client can resubmit the failed requests in a way that is rate limiting.

**Write it as.** `429 Too Many Requests` · `resubmit the failed requests`

**Scope.** REST APIs.

> "When request submissions exceed the steady-state request rate and burst limits, API Gateway begins to throttle requests. Clients may receive `429 Too Many Requests` error responses at this point. Upon catching such exceptions, the client can resubmit the failed requests in a way that is rate limiting."
> — [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### api-gateway-throttling-account-level-default-rps-burst

**Claim.** By default, API Gateway limits the steady-state requests per second (RPS) and the burst (the maximum bucket size) across all APIs within an AWS account, per Region; the burst limit is the target maximum number of concurrent request submissions API Gateway fulfills before returning 429 errors.

**Write it as.** `steady-state requests per second (RPS)` · `across all APIs within an AWS account` · `the maximum bucket size`

**Scope.** per account, per Region, all APIs; default; not adjustable.

> "By default, API Gateway limits the steady-state requests per second (RPS) across all APIs within an AWS account, per Region. It also limits the burst (that is, the maximum bucket size) across all APIs within an AWS account, per Region. In API Gateway, the burst limit represents the target maximum number of concurrent request submissions that API Gateway will fulfill before returning `429 Too Many Requests` error responses."
> — [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### api-gateway-throttling-account-limit-increase-on-request

**Claim.** Per-account throttling limits apply to all APIs in an account in a specified Region; the account-level rate limit can be increased upon request, and these limits cannot be higher than the AWS throttling limits.

**Write it as.** `increased upon request` · `can't be higher than the AWS throttling limits` · `shorter timeouts and smaller payloads`

**Scope.** per account, per Region.

> "Per-account limits are applied to all APIs in an account in a specified Region. The account-level rate limit can be increased upon request - higher limits are possible with APIs that have shorter timeouts and smaller payloads. To request an increase of account-level throttling limits per Region, contact the AWS Support Center. For more information, see Amazon API Gateway quotas. Note that these limits can't be higher than the AWS throttling limits."
> — [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### api-gateway-throttling-application-order

**Claim.** API Gateway applies throttling-related settings in this order: per-client or per-method limits in a usage plan, then per-method limits set for an API stage, then account-level throttling per Region, then AWS Regional throttling.

**Write it as.** `per-client or per-method throttling limits` · `AWS Regional throttling`

**Scope.** REST APIs.

> "API Gateway applies your throttling-related settings in the following order: Per-client or per-method throttling limits that you set for an API stage in a usage plan Per-method throttling limits that you set for an API stage Account-level throttling per Region AWS Regional throttling"
> — [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### api-gateway-throttling-aws-limits-not-changeable

**Claim.** AWS throttling limits are applied across all accounts and clients in a Region, are set by AWS, and cannot be changed by a customer.

**Write it as.** `across all accounts and clients in a Region` · `can't be changed by a customer`

**Scope.** per Region, all accounts and clients.

> "AWS throttling limits are applied across all accounts and clients in a Region. These limit settings exist to prevent your API—and your account—from being overwhelmed by too many requests. These limits are set by AWS and can't be changed by a customer."
> — [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### api-gateway-throttling-token-bucket-per-account-region

**Claim.** API Gateway throttles requests using the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request, and it examines the rate and a burst of request submissions against all APIs in your account, per Region.

**Scope.** per account, per Region.

> "API Gateway throttles requests to your API using the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request. Specifically, API Gateway examines the rate and a burst of request submissions against all APIs in your account, per Region. In the token bucket algorithm, a burst can allow pre-defined overrun of those limits, but other factors can also cause limits to be overrun in some cases."

You can also specify a throttling burst, which is the capacity of the token bucket."
